title: Tokyo
dek: A food-first long weekend for six — one Saturday splurge dinner worth the friction, everything else built to stay easy.
verified: ⚠ Pass A + Pass B reconciled — offline verify pending, networked verify and citation audit not yet run. Every fact below is sourced, but nothing here is final.

entry.visa: Visa-free for tourism, stays up to 90 days. Japan's planned ETA system (JESTA) does not apply yet — implementation targets FY2028, after this trip.
entry.note: Assumed US passport — the traveler's nationality wasn't confirmed at intake (see the traveler questions). If any traveler holds a different passport, check that country's own entry rule. mofa.go.jp and moj.go.jp both blocked automated verification in this pass (403) — reconfirm at mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html before departure.

items.native: [食材]アレルギーがあります
items.note: Fill in the allergen (e.g. ピーナッツ peanut, 小麦 wheat, 甲殻類 shellfish) before アレルギーがあります. Say it when seated, before ordering — pair with a written allergy card for clarity.
Broader than the allergy phrase — covers dietary restrictions and preferences too.
Give the name the booking is under right after this.
Useful for walk-ins — staff will ask party size (nan-mei sama desu ka) before seating.
Standard way to get a server's attention at izakaya and counter seating, where nobody comes to the table unprompted.

items.native: いただきます／ごちそうさまでした
items.note: Said before the first bite and after the last — genuinely used, not just textbook politeness.
Most sit-down restaurants pay at the table or a front register on the way out, not tableside by card machine.

items.situation: Do you have an English menu?
items.native: 英語のメニューはありますか？
items.romanization: eigo no menyū wa arimasu ka?
